findings.title: Comparison identity omits hardware/model/resources/client settings; Train selection and comparison table treat mismatched runs as comparable with neither refusal nor an UNVERIFIED comparability status
findings.confidence: high: code fact, witness W2 confirmed on both Pythons
findings.lines: 263-266 provenance requires only offered_trace_sha256; 510-512 select_train_fixed identity = trace sha + all_offered; 584-588 comparison_table identity = trace sha, all_offered, envelope_scope, refusal text 'incomparable'; 606-609 table output has no comparability field; 677-682 adapter preserves host/gpu/models/gateway_launch/backend_launch_provenance/code_sha256/packages but nothing compares them; 27-28 and 68-72 qualification/claims_not_made are silent on hardware/resource comparability; test_nominal_metrics.py 342 and 365-372 identity tests cover only sha/scope
findings.effect: Arms measured on different hosts, GPUs, served model assets, gateway/backend launch settings (other than the arm budget), code/package versions, clock domains, offered windows or client generation settings (e.g. per-row requested_ignore_eos) pass select_train_fixed and comparison_table whenever they share a trace sha and count (and scope). The Train fixed choice can be decided by an environment difference that is attributed to the budget, and the table presents the rows side by side; the only refusal text ('incomparable') implies that accepted tables are comparable. The author definition 'comparison_identity: measured arms must share offered trace sha256, all-offered count and envelope scope' is implemented as written; the defect is that it is narrower than the required comparability (same hardware/model/resources/SLO/workload/window) and the output does not say so. On the adapter path the verified trace.json sha (838-839) binds the offered requests, the trace model path string, duration and purpose, and per-arm checks require cache_policy disabled (853-854) and gateway MODEL_NAME equal to the trace model path (804-807); host, GPU, served-model asset fingerprint behind that path, backend launch settings, code/packages and client generation settings are still never compared across arms. compute()-direct producers bind nothing beyond a self-declared sha.
findings.reproducer: W2 in witness_metrics01.py (logs witness-py314-01.log, witness-py312-01.log): fixed16 vs fixed32 Train runs with the same request id, sha and count; provenance manifest host/gpu/models A vs B; different clock_domain; fixed32 row requested_ignore_eos true. Rows have identical timings; natural_slo_good is fixed16 1 vs fixed32 0 solely because of the ignore_eos client setting. Result: select_train_fixed SELECTED fixed16 decided_by primary_natural_slo_good (the budget 'choice' is decided entirely by a non-budget condition); comparison_table(purpose=train) ACCEPTED; no comparability key and no comparability/hardware wording anywhere in the table.
findings.liveness: table path live now (tables do not need natural SLO); selection path latent while G-SLO refuses natural SLO
findings.disposition_recommendation: FIX OR LABEL BEFORE ANY CROSS-ARM TABLE OR SELECTION IS CITED: define a comparability record (host, GPU model/count, served model asset plus alias fingerprint, backend and gateway launch settings except the arm budget, code_sha256/packages, client generation config including requested_ignore_eos and max_tokens policy, clock domain, offered_duration_s and relative schedule) in normalized provenance; select_train_fixed and comparison_table refuse on mismatch, or emit comparability UNVERIFIED with the unchecked field list and stop calling accepted tables comparable; add a regression test with equal sha/count but different host/gpu.

findings.title: Eval table accepts any SELECTED dict as the Train selection: no Train/Eval provenance binding, no same-trace leakage detector, selection provenance dropped from the table
findings.confidence: high: code fact, witness W3 (main and secondary) confirmed on both Pythons
findings.lines: 589-591 train_selection check is only dict, status SELECTED and selected_arm in FIXED_BUDGETS; 599-605 alias built from selected_arm alone; 607-609 output omits the selection's offered_trace_sha256, decided_by, candidates and rule; 525 'must be frozen before any Eval replay' is text only (no freeze time or artifact hash input); 235-236 and 205-211 purpose and static_fixed control are self-declared for compute()-direct producers; 506 refusal wording 'not a verified static fixed runtime' although verification exists only in the adapter (774-796, 851-852)
findings.effect: An Eval table can carry a train_selected_fixed ALIAS whose selection was computed on the Eval trace relabelled purpose train (selection sha equal to the Eval table sha, a cheap positive reuse signal that is not checked) or on nothing at all (a hand-made minimal dict is accepted). The alias then reports an Eval-optimised choice (optimistic max-of-two bias) under a Train-selection label, and readers cannot audit decided_by (tie_2 means no data-driven choice) because the table drops it. Unequal hashes would still not prove disjointness, consistent with the module's own claims_not_made; equality is positive evidence of reuse.
findings.reproducer: W3: Train selection (tie_2_lower_budget, fixed16) and Eval runs share sha 'w3'*32; comparison_table(purpose=eval) ACCEPTED, alias ALIAS of fixed16, selection_sha_equals_eval_table_sha true, no selection key in the table. Secondary: {'status': 'SELECTED', 'selected_arm': 'fixed32'} ACCEPTED as ALIAS of fixed32.
findings.liveness: forged/minimal-dict path live whenever a caller supplies train_selection; genuine Train selection latent while G-SLO refuses natural SLO
findings.disposition_recommendation: FIX BEFORE ANY EVAL TABLE SHOWS train_selected_fixed: require a complete select_train_fixed result (rule, candidates, offered_trace_sha256, scope) plus a frozen selection artifact hash/time recorded before the Eval run; refuse when the selection sha equals the Eval identity; carry selection sha, decided_by and candidates into the alias row; otherwise label the alias 'selection provenance UNVERIFIED'. If the unread coordinator already binds this, cite that binding.

findings.title: sent_at < scheduled_at (early or non-causal send) is accepted, earns scheduled-origin TTFT and natural-SLO credit, and is invisible in send_lag_s
findings.confidence: high: code fact, witness W1 confirmed on both Pythons; incidence in real producers unverified
findings.lines: 181-184 _validate_row checks first >= sent, first >= scheduled, terminal >= sent and first, but never sent >= scheduled; 460 and 474-475 with 127-150 send_lag_s reports n, p50/p95/p99 and max only; score_http.py 10 and 34 TTFT measured from scheduled_at with limit 0.5 s; test_nominal_metrics.py 152 the only sent-before-scheduled case also moves first before scheduled, so the first >= scheduled rule refuses it and masks the gap
findings.effect: A row sent before its offered arrival gives the server a head start, so scheduled-origin TTFT (the primary TTFT origin and the natural-SLO origin) is understated and an SLO miss can become credit. A minority of early rows never shows in send_lag_s: the nearest-rank p50 is negative only if at least ceil(n/2) rows are early and max only if all are. The only residual trace is an unflagged order-statistic inversion (client-send TTFT quantile above the scheduled TTFT quantile, impossible when every sent >= scheduled). Plausible mechanisms (unverified; sources unread): a coordinator releasing arrivals at control-tick boundaries before their scheduled times, or sent and scheduled stamped from different clocks by a compute()-direct producer.
findings.reproducer: W1: rows (scheduled, sent) = (11.0, 10.5), (12.0, 12.0), (13.0, 13.0) with first = scheduled + 0.125, terminal = scheduled + 0.25, 5 tokens. Result: ACCEPTED; natural_slo_good 3 although the early row's first - sent = 0.625 > 0.5; send_lag p50 = p95 = p99 = max = 0.0 and no min/negative key; conditional_client_send p99 0.625 > conditional_scheduled p99 0.125.
findings.liveness: TTFT understatement live for any producer; SLO credit live once SLO fields exist
findings.disposition_recommendation: FIX: refuse sent_at < scheduled_at - tol in _validate_row with a documented tolerance (clock resolution or a declared small bound, with the count of rows inside the tolerance reported); add send_lag min and n_negative; add a test isolating sent < scheduled with first >= scheduled.

findings.title: All-offered denominator is not bound to the offered trace for compute()-direct producers; compared arms are not checked for the same request-id set
findings.confidence: high: schema fact; cross-arm id mismatch confirmed by W3 secondary flag on both Pythons
findings.lines: 49-54 ROW_KEYS/RUN_KEYS carry no offered count or request-id digest; 250-251 only uniqueness is checked; 473 all_offered = len(rows); 510-512 and 584-588 cross-arm checks compare counts, never ids; contrast adapter 717-718 and 860-864 one-to-one, order-checked coverage
findings.effect: A compute()-direct producer (the G-LOOP coordinator journal path in the author report, or native client capture) that drops rows, e.g. unresolved/unknown or not-yet-written requests, reports a smaller all_offered and inflated slo_attainment_fraction / delivered_fraction / lower rejection_rate with no refusal for a single run, for the only measured arm of a table, or when arms drop the same number of rows. Two arms with different request-id sets but equal sha and count are accepted as one cohort. The author definition 'denominator: all offered rows (one per offered request id, unique)' is therefore enforced only on the adapter path.
findings.reproducer: W3 secondary: Eval arms with request ids ['w3-e16'] vs ['w3-e32'], same sha and count, comparison_table ACCEPTED (f3_cross_arm_request_id_mismatch_accepted true). The dropped-row case follows directly from the schema (no field can carry the offered count) and was not separately executed.
findings.liveness: latent on the adapter path (protected), live for compute()-direct producers
findings.disposition_recommendation: FIX BEFORE compute()-DIRECT PRODUCERS ARE SCORED: add offered_count and an ordered request-id digest derived from the frozen offered tape to normalized provenance; validate_run checks len(rows) and the digest; select_train_fixed and comparison_table compare the digest, not only the count.

findings.title: Row timestamps are not bound to the declared offered window or envelope; the offered_cohort_observed envelope definition is enforced only by the adapter
findings.confidence: high: code fact, witness W4 confirmed on both Pythons
findings.lines: 241-243 validate_run only checks that the envelope covers the offered window; 153-190 no row time is compared with offered_start/offered end/envelope; 55-58 scope definition 'offered start to the later of offered end and last observed terminal'; 330, 354 and 449 wall-envelope rates and the overhead fraction divide by envelope_s; score_http.py 51 in-window goodput only checks terminal_at <= window end; contrast adapter 872 envelope_end = max(end, every terminal)
findings.effect: A compute()-direct producer can (a) include rows scheduled outside the offered window (warmup or extra requests), which enter all_offered and are credited as in-window natural-SLO goodput, and (b) declare envelope_end before the last terminal, which shortens envelope_s below the scope's own definition and inflates wall-envelope delivered, SLO-goodput and token rates and the overhead fraction while windows.envelope_scope_label still states the later-of definition.
findings.reproducer: W4: offered [10, 15], envelope [10, 15]; rows scheduled 3.0 (terminal 3.25, natural good) and 14.0 (terminal 20.0). Result: ACCEPTED; natural_slo_good 1 and in_window_slo_goodput_rps 0.2 credit the pre-window row; envelope_s 5.0 versus 10.0 under the label definition; wall_envelope_delivered_rps 0.4 versus 0.2.
findings.liveness: latent on the adapter path (872; scheduled = measurement_start + arrival_seconds), live for compute()-direct producers
findings.disposition_recommendation: FIX: validate_run refuses scheduled_at outside [offered_start, offered_start + offered_duration_s]; for offered_cohort_observed require envelope_end >= max observed terminal_at (or derive it as the adapter does); for full_wall require every observation inside [envelope_start, envelope_end].

findings.title: Group fairness summaries drop group sizes: unweighted Jain/min_over_max over up to three groups, no k or per-group n in the table, worst rejection without group or n
findings.confidence: high: code fact; analytic path, not executed
findings.lines: 387-400 _spread is unweighted over non-empty groups with no minimum n (carries groups_used and k, no per-group n); 413 worst_group_rejection_rate has no group name or n, unlike the conditional p95 at 414-416; 554-555 summary/table carry only the two Jain values; the author report text 'worst group rejection and conditional p95 with n' holds only for the p95
findings.effect: Jain is the same for a 1-request group and a 30-request group with the same rate: slo_attainment_fraction (1, 1, 0) gives Jain 4/6 = 0.667 whether the failing group has n = 1 or n = 30. Table readers comparing jain_slo_attainment across arms see neither k nor n; with Train class counts 33/26/29 (nominal_scenario.py 38), a few requests move a group rate by several percentage points.
findings.reproducer: analytic: three non-empty groups with rates (1.0, 1.0, 0.0), Jain = (2)^2 / (3 * (1 + 1 + 0)) = 0.667 independent of group n; only jain_slo_attainment reaches the summary
findings.liveness: live for slo_attainment Jain only when SLO fields exist; delivered_fraction Jain live now
findings.disposition_recommendation: LABEL AND CARRY: add k and per-group n_offered to the spread and table summary, name the worst rejection group with its n, and state that Jain over unweighted group rates has no uncertainty and should not be ranked across arms without n.

findings.title: Rate labels: 'actual wall envelope' on a lower-bound envelope (so rates are upper bounds on full-wall rates) and delivered-only token rates whose qualifiers are dropped from the table summary
findings.lines: 67 ENVELOPE_LABEL 'actual wall envelope: count / (envelope_end - envelope_start)'; 329-332 and 354-355 the label is attached under every scope, including offered_cohort_observed, the adapter's only scope (873); 55-58 that scope is a lower bound on the full wall; 340-365 token lower/upper/exact cover fate complete rows only, undelivered tokens are reported separately and unbounded when usage is missing, and the upper bound assumes the endpoint never exceeds max_output_tokens (unstated); 537 and 549-557 the summary carries envelope_scope but not the bound direction, and carries token-rate dicts without 'delivered only' or the premise

Token rates with exact true describe delivered rows only and can be read as total generated tokens.

findings.disposition_recommendation: LABEL: scope-dependent envelope label (e.g. 'offered-cohort observed envelope: lower bound on full wall, rates are upper bounds'); carry 'delivered rows only; upper assumes endpoint-enforced max_tokens' beside token rates in the summary.

findings.confidence: high as a code fact; impact unverified (validate_snapshot and callers unread)

findings.title: Forecast arrivals use a fixed 15 s stationary horizon per snapshot with no offered-window input
findings.confidence: high as a code fact; impact unverified (FutureOffer offset semantics and the planner's use of the tail unread)
findings.lines: 42 HORIZON_S = 15.0 with comment 'scored 5s plus contention-only 10s tail'; 141-158 Poisson(88/5 = 17.6 per s) offsets from 0 up to 15 s regenerated for every snapshot; 124-125 no offered-window start/end or snapshot position input; 43-49 ASSUMPTIONS omit the horizon/window alignment; nominal_workload.py 40 public protocol window duration_ns = 5 s
findings.effect: If offsets are snapshot-relative, a snapshot t seconds into the 5 s window forecasts about 17.6 * (10 + t) expected arrivals (176 to 264) after the public window end that will never be offered, so predicted contention is systematically above the known protocol late in the window. This is model misspecification, not leakage (the window end is public). The line-42 comment presumes a horizon starting at the window start.
findings.liveness: depends on unread planner use of the 'contention-only' tail
findings.disposition_recommendation: DOCUMENT OR FIX: pass the public offered-window end into make_scenario and truncate arrivals at it, or state the stationary continuation in ASSUMPTIONS and in the forecast output; quantify only in a later authorized experiment.
